page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at top left, page number at top right. No marginal notes. Catchword at lower right.

main_text.p: mofynis viuentes, non esse in statu salutis. Combus sit etiam, uidente curia Romana, libellum pestifi-rum (cur non & libelli authores?) quo author asserebat statum gratiae non a lege Euangelij, sed a lege spiritus procedere. Quae opinio ex libris Ioannis abbatis sumpta dicebatur. Hic autem liber a sectatoribus Euangelium aeternum dicebatur. Haec Platina ex Ioannes de Parma ordinis fratrum Minorum, minister generalis, qui in gymnasio Parisiensi Sententias legerat, doctrinam abbatis Ioachimi sequebatur: haec Antoninus. Contra Guilhelmum de S. Amore, & alios pios theologos, his temporibus declamitant ac scribebant, Thomas Aquinas, Albertus Magnus, Bonaventura de Balneo regio, Humbertus Viennensis, Hugo Birchinensis, Helias Brunetus, & alij mendicantium fraterculorum plures. Ex eodem Antonino. Expar te altera Guilhelmus de S. Amore, Gallus, scriptum Defensorium scripturae & Ecclesiae contra pericula imminentia Ecclesiae generali per hypocritas ac pseudoprædicatores, penetrantes domos, ociosos & curiosos, gyrovagos, lib. 4. De periculis nouissimorum temporum, lib. 1. De quinquaginta signis pseudoprophetantium, lib. 1. Quaestiones de mendicitate, contra Bonaventuram, lib 1. Et sermones aliquot. Gerardus Sagarellus, Italus, m doctor

page.notes: Several words are doubtful because of the faded and damaged paper: the opening word "mofynis" (possibly "mosynis"), "effe" (long s printed as ff, read as esse), the hyphenated "pestifi-rum", and the names "Birchinensis" and "Balneo". The line "Expar te" has no printed hyphen at its line end. The letter "m" before "doctor" at the foot is read as a stray mark and may be the start of a word. The text is set as one paragraph because no new indent is visible. Proper names and titles should be checked against the scan.
